name: MemoryLedger
summary: What the agent stored, recalled or forgot — and where it came from.

a11y.apg: disclosure — provenance is a native <details>, so opening and closing is the platform's, keyboard included. Ordered list because the order is the ledger.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: Enter, which opens a record's detail — a native <details>/<summary> again. Space is declared and did not toggle it in Chromium build 1194; see InterAgentMessage for the direct measurement.

props.name: records
props.description: One entry per posting, not per memory. A ledger is append-only: "forgotten" does not drop the row, it records the forgetting — and that row is exactly what you go looking for when an agent stops knowing something.

notes: The only component of Part H with no open-source reference: Letta's ADE ships only its server, mem0's OpenMemory is being discontinued, and mem0's own panel is cloud-only. Measured 08/08/2026, reconfirmed 09/08/2026. It is built from registered research plus composition — the research is in REFERENCES.md.

The three scopes (episodic, semantic, procedural) are the vocabulary that became standard across vendors in 2026. Letta's three tiers (core, recall, archival) were deliberately left out: they are one product's architecture, and freezing them here would tie the contract to a single vendor.

It does NOT wrap DataGrid. data-grid.tsx lives in its own subpath because it carries @tanstack/react-table as an OPTIONAL peer (check 19), and agents.tsx ships through the light barrel — importing it would make anyone who installed the library for the Button start needing the table. Sorting and filtering a ledger is composed in the application; the catalogue example shows it.
